text: ← All problemsThe quadratic universal-container formula for fixed polyominoesIdentify square lattice cells with points of $\mathbb Z^2$, adjacent when their Manhattan distance is one. A polyomino is a finite nonempty edge-connected set of cells. Let $a(n)$ be the least cardinality of a finite connected container $C\subset\mathbb Z^2$ such that every $n$-cell polyomino $P$ admits an integer translation $t$ with $P+t\subseteq C$. Orientations are fixed: every rotated or reflected shape is an input in its own right, and a placement allows translation only. Holes are permitted. Formula proposed in OEIS A395495. Is $a(n)=\frac{n^2-n+6}{2}\qquad\text{for every integer }n\ge4?$ This record concerns that universal formula, not a claim of optimality for any smaller proposed container.ReferencesPeter Exley, OEIS A395495, proposed formula for the translation-only universal-container problem, n ≥ 4. https://oeis.org/A39549500Posted by MJ KangPosted just nowEdit problemDelete problemProgress summaryRefreshNever refreshedNothing recorded yet.
